190: Rabbi Elazar said, "Fortunate is the share of the righteous: Yaakov fled from before his brother, and he chanced upon a well. Once the well saw him, the water made itself known to its master and went up towards him and rejoiced with him. And it was there that he was matched with his spouse. Moshe fled from before Pharaoh, and he chanced upon that same well. So the water saw him and made itself known to its master and went up towards him. And it was there that he was matched with his spouse.

Was there any difference between Moshe and Yaakov? It is written about Yaakov (Genesis 29:10), "When Yaakov saw Rachel, etc., he stepped near and rolled the stone, etc." What is written about Moshe? "Then the shepherds came and chased them away; so Moshe got up and saved them, etc." (Exodus 2:17). Once Moshe saw that the water was coming up towards him, he certainly knew that he would be matched with his match there. Moreover, the holy spirit never ever left him; and through it, he knew that Tzipporah would be his spouse. Moshe said, "Yaakov certainly came here; and [when] the water went up towards him, he chanced upon a man who brought him into his house and gave him everything he needed. I too will be like this!"
